sections.title: Interatomic potential
sections.html:
Screened second-generation REBO (REBO2+S): Brenner et al. (2002) second-generation reactive empirical bond-order potential with the environment-dependent screening functions of Pastewka et al. (2008, 2013). The authoritative implementation is Atomistica's Rebo2Scr (Fortran, v1.2.7, default parameters, dihedral term off). The production engine TorchRebo2Scr is an exact PyTorch port of that kernel: repulsive VR, attractive VA, angular bond order with the coordination-switched g(cos θ) splines, the PCC bicubic and FCC tricubic tables (with derivative tables), conjugation counter, all four cut-off functions (inner 1.95–2.25 Å, attractive/repulsive 2.18–2.82 Å, bond order 1.87–2.76 Å, neighbour/conjugation 1.22–4.00 Å) and the elliptical screening Sij = Πk exp[−((Cmax−C)/(C−Cmin))²] with Cmin=1, Cmax=2. Forces are exact gradients (autograd), the virial is dE/dε. Agreement with Atomistica: ≤1e-13 eV/atom, ≤1e-12 eV/Å (float64).

Nothing in the mechanics comes from springs, beams, continuum models, rigid bodies or learned surrogates.

sections.title: Numerical modes
sections.html: Fast discovery mode: MPS (Apple GPU) or CUDA, float32 — used for the campaign. Reference mode: CPU float64 — bit-identical to Atomistica; used for validation and cross-checks. Quantified differences (fast vs reference): energies ~1e-6 eV/atom, forces ~1e-4 eV/Å, 2D stress ~1e-5 N/m — far below the minimisation tolerance (0.02 eV/Å) and the stress scales of interest (1–40 N/m).

sections.title: Structures
sections.html: All structures are explicit carbon atoms in orthorhombic periodic supercells (x,y periodic; z vacuum) represented as ASE Atoms, generated from a pristine graphene sheet at the REBO2+S lattice constant a0 = 2.4602 Å by atom removal (pores, slits, cracks, vacancies) followed by pruning of dangling atoms and relaxation. Every structure carries its generator, parameters and seed; export formats: extxyz, xyz, ASE traj, LAMMPS data, CIF, POSCAR.

sections.title: Athermal quasi-static tensile protocol (AQS)
sections.html: Uniaxial engineering strain along x in increments of 1% before the first bond-breaking event (bisected to 0.125% around that event, using a 400-iteration trial relaxation to detect bond loss) and 0.5% afterwards, affine mapping of positions, FIRE relaxation of all atoms to |F|max < 0.02 eV/Å, transverse cell relaxed to σyy = 0 (secant iterations, trust region 0.5%), 2D stress from the virial per area (N/m). The reference state is the zero-stress relaxed cell. A structure is stopped when the bond network no longer spans the loading direction, when the stress collapses below 5% of the peak after damage, or at 35% strain.

sections.title: Damage and connectivity analysis
sections.html: The reactive potential has no bond table; for analysis two carbon atoms are considered bonded if r < 2.0 Å (between the equilibrium bond length 1.42 Å and the inner cut-off 1.95–2.25 Å). Bond loss between consecutive converged states is recorded with the strain and location of the event; persistence is enforced in post-processing. Damage localisation L = 1 − H/Hmax with H the Shannon entropy of the damage-event positions on an 8×8 grid over the cell (L = 0 uniform, L = 1 fully localised).

sections.title: Metrics and units
sections.html: 2D modulus Y2D (N/m, linear fit ε ≤ 2%), 2D strength σmax (N/m), strain at peak, first-damage strain, failure strain (stress < 10% of peak or loss of spanning), work to failure W = ∫σ dε (J/m², a simulation-derived energy-absorption proxy, not a fracture toughness), specific work per atom (eV), post-peak load retention, number of damage steps, damage localisation, fracture-mode classification. 3D-equivalent stresses are never reported implicitly; if needed, σ3D = σ2D/t with t = 0.335 nm would apply.

sections.title: Known limitations of the model
sections.html: REBO2(+S) underestimates the in-plane stiffness of graphene (Y2D = 245 N/m vs ≈340 N/m experiment) and overestimates the Poisson ratio (0.39 vs ≈0.17); intrinsic strengths (37.7 N/m zigzag, 30.5 N/m armchair) are close to experiment (≈42 N/m). Under zigzag tension the homogeneous lattice shows a bistable transverse response above ≈16% strain (soft-mode instability of the model). Screening switch-on/off produces steep (but continuous) force features when an atom crosses the screening ellipse of a neighbouring pair. All results are properties of this classical model; no claim of synthesizability is made.
